messages:
Aisha: Quick sync — updating the battlecard messaging for next week's webinar + the benchmark post. Need decisions on 3 claims before EOD.
Diego: I can do wording for the field-facing bullets. Which claims are we prioritizing?
Aisha: 1) Unified runtime advantage vs cloud AI endpoints, 2) predictable economics vs pay-per-call LLM APIs, 3) private deployment story vs infra vendors.
Lena: For the webinar hook we should lead with "predictable inference economics" not "lower cost" — resonates with platform teams.
Sam: Agreed. Sales team sees "lower cost" debated in deals. Predictable throughput + SLOs is a stronger close.
Jon: For the benchmark narrative, can we include a short table? e.g., CloudX endpoint avg p90 latency 320ms, Redwood hosted p90 120ms (same model). Want to be careful about naming specifics.
Diego: We should avoid raw numbers in the battlecard that could be parsed as a hard SLA. Use ranges and asterisks: "~2-3x lower p90 in typical configs" and link to lab notes.
Lena: Nice. For infra vendors claim: "We provide a unified control plane across hosted, dedicated, and private — no vendor lock-in on serving runtime" — too wordy?
Sam: Shorten to "Same API and controls across hosted, reserved, and on-prem — deploy anywhere with consistent performance"
Aisha: Love that. Now inbound routing — marketing wants to route webinar signups to AE queue vs SDR depending on usage intent. We proposed an A/B test using the registration form question.
Jon: Proposed routing logic: if checkbox "planning to deploy in next 90 days" -> AE, else -> SDR nurture. Also tag responses with "interest:dedicated" or "interest:private".
Diego: For battlecards, include 3 quick rebuttals per competitor bucket (Cloud AI platforms, LLM APIs, infra vendors). Short snippets: 1- liner, 1 technical backup, 1 field proof.
Lena: I'll draft the Cloud AI platform rebuttals today. Sam can add the field proof examples (customer quotes).
Sam: I'll pull 2 customer quotes: one about hitting latency SLOs on Dedicated, one on switching from managed endpoints to Redwood Private for compliance.
Aisha: Marco-bot, deploy the latest benchmark asset to drive link for the battlecard.
marco-bot: Uploaded: /internal-assets/benchmarks/2026-03-18-inference-bench-v3.pdf :thumbsup:
Diego: Can we include a tiny code snippet for the battlecard showing same API call across environments?
Jon: Yes, keep it 3 lines. Example: 
```
POST /v1/generate 
{ "model": "redwood-3b", "input": "Summarize..." }
```
Lena: Also need a one-line headline for the webinar slide: "Keep inference predictable: performance, cost, control" — thoughts?
Sam: Maybe swap order to emphasize control: "Control, predictability, and performance for real-world LLMs"
Aisha: Good. Action items: Lena — finalize Cloud AI bucket rebuttals (today). Diego — write infra vendor rebuttals and the 3-line code snippet (EOD). Sam — pull customer quotes + tag approvals (tomorrow AM). Jon — generate the short benchmark blurb and publish link into the battlecard (today). I'll update the inbound routing A/B test doc and send to growth.
Diego: Tiny copy tweak suggestion for field snippet: replace "vendor lock-in" with "serving lock-in" — more specific.
Lena: Yep. Use "serving lock-in".
Aisha: If no objections, we'll ship this iteration to #field-docs by 5pm and include the webinar slide deck. :rocket:
Sam: No objections. :+1:
Jon: On it.
marco-bot: Reminder: battlecard template v2 saved to /templates/battlecard-v2.md
Aisha: Thanks all — short, sharp, and publish.
